title: Integral closedness lifts the finite minimal-prime decomposition to domain factors
statement: Let $R$ be a reduced commutative ring with finitely many minimal prime ideals. Suppose $R$ is integrally closed [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] in its total ring of fractions $Q(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then for some integer $n\ge 0$ there are commutative integral domains $A_i$ for $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ and a ring isomorphism $R\simeq\prod_i A_i$. No integral closedness of the factors is asserted.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), proof, second and third paragraphs; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030C

proof.text: For a minimal prime p, let S be the finite set of the other minimal primes. Minimality implies p is not contained in any r in S. Finite prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] gives b in p outside all r in S. The finite intersection of S is not contained in p: otherwise primality of p implies one r in S is contained in p, contradicting minimality. Choose a in this intersection outside p. Every minimal prime contains ab, so ab=0 by reducedness and the intersection-of-minimal-primes formula [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]. The sum a+b avoids every minimal prime, hence is a nonzerodivisor by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-zerodivisors-union-minimal-primes].

Set x=a/(a+b) in the total fraction ring. Clearing the invertible denominator twice and using ab=0 proves x*x=x. Thus x is integral, being a root of the monic polynomial T(T-1) [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Integral closedness gives e in R mapping to x, and injectivity yields e(a+b)=a and (1-e)(a+b)=b. For every other minimal prime q, primality and a+b not in q imply e in q. Likewise 1-e is in p. Hence p and q are coprime, with the explicit witnesses 1-e and e. This constructs the separating coordinate idempotents directly, without first decomposing the entire total fraction ring.

Enumerate minimalPrimes R by Fin n using its finiteness. Their intersection is the nilradical and hence zero by reducedness [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]. Apply Mathlib Ideal.quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotient to the pairwise coprime family and compose with Ideal.quotEquivOfEq and RingEquiv.quotientBot to obtain R isomorphic to the product of R/p. Every quotient is a domain because p is prime. Package these explicitly defined quotients as CommRingCat objects. The same Chinese remainder theorem handles the empty family, so no nontriviality assumption or separate zero-ring construction is required.
